title: JACC: Leveraging HPC Meta-Programming and Performance Portability with the Just-in-Time and LLVM-based Julia Language
problem: Writing high-performance HPC code that efficiently targets multiple CPU and GPU architectures requires separate implementations for each platform. Developers need a unified programming model that maintains performance across heterogeneous systems without code duplication and maintenance burden.
motivation: Performance portability is critical for HPC as supercomputing facilities deploy diverse hardware, and a single code path that runs efficiently across CPUs, GPUs, and accelerators reduces development effort and enables better code reuse.
method: JACC is a system built on Julia (a programming language) that lets you write high-performance code once and have it automatically run fast on both CPUs and GPUs. It works by compiling your code at runtime—called just-in-time compilation—and using Julia's meta-programming features (code that writes other code) to automatically generate optimized versions for each specific hardware platform. The system relies on LLVM, a compiler technology that converts the generated code into efficient machine instructions for different CPU and GPU architectures.
key_novelty: The core idea is a high-level programming model where you write a single piece of code that runs nearly as efficiently on CPUs and GPUs as code hand-optimized separately for each specific hardware platform.
contributions: First performance-portable Julia model for HPC accelerators with high-level abstractions
Unified frontend across diverse Julia backends enabling multi-target code generation
Demonstration of negligible performance overhead versus vendor-specific implementations
Validation on major US DOE supercomputers (Aurora, Frontier, Perlmutter) with HPC benchmarks including HPCCG and HARVEY

metrics.speedup: GPU speedups maintained vs vendor-specific solutions
metrics.other: Negligible overhead relative to vendor implementations
